github_docs_as_code_fit.rationale: Everything is repo files: MDX content, Joi-validated frontmatter, sidebars-as-code, single TS config, i18n as file copies. Git drives lastUpdate metadata via a pluggable VCS abstraction; editUrl links to GitHub; first-party GitHub Pages deploy command. No database or content API exists at all.
github_docs_as_code_fit.evidence: packages/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/src/index.ts (filesystem loadContent); packages/docusaurus-types/src/config.d.ts (VcsConfig, gitEagerVcs); packages/docusaurus/src/commands/deploy.ts; theme-classic EditThisPage component

ai_integration_extensibility.rationale: No native AI features (correct for static-first), but the file-based model makes AI-generated MDX a first-class citizen: unknown frontmatter keys pass validation (provenance metadata), global MDXComponents registration removes import boilerplate from generated files, and the typed plugin lifecycle plus deterministic build give a strong validation gate. Docked one point: MDX v3 strictness is a real failure mode for LLM output, and there is no built-in content-AST policy tooling.
ai_integration_extensibility.evidence: packages/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/src/frontMatter.ts (.unknown() schema); packages/docusaurus-theme-classic/src/theme/MDXComponents/index.tsx; packages/docusaurus-types/src/plugin.d.ts (lifecycle); website/docusaurus.config.ts ~line 676 (DocSearch Ask AI, optional only)

architecture_simplicity.rationale: Operator-facing surface is small (one config, one CLI, static output, no servers), fitting the one-engineer rule. Internally it is a heavy React SPA-hydration stack with a large npm tree, webpack/Rspack duality, Node >=24.14 and React 19 requirements — more machinery than minimal SSGs, and swizzling adds an upgrade-coupling layer.
architecture_simplicity.evidence: packages/docusaurus/package.json (engines node >=24.14, react ^19.2.5, webpack ^5.106.2); packages/docusaurus-bundler/src/currentBundler.ts (dual bundler); pnpm-lock.yaml size; 38-package monorepo under packages/

structured_content_ia.rationale: Best-in-class docs IA: multi-instance docs plugin (hard canonical/generated separation, dogfooded upstream), autogenerated or explicit sidebars, categories with generated index pages, tags, breadcrumbs, snapshot versioning per instance, draft/unlisted visibility states, rich validated frontmatter controlling slugs, ordering and pagination.
structured_content_ia.evidence: website/docusaurus.config.ts:369 (id community instance); packages/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/src/sidebars/generator.ts; src/versions/; src/frontMatter.ts (sidebar_position, displayed_sidebar, ContentVisibilitySchema)

security_governance.rationale: Static serving plane eliminates runtime attack surface; upstream governance is strong (CodeQL, dependency review, supply-chain workflow, Meta OSS backing, MIT license). Docked: very large npm dependency surface at build time, MDX is executable code (generated JSX ships to browsers), and no SECURITY.md in-repo (reports go via Meta's program).
security_governance.evidence: .github/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml, dependency-review.yml, security-supply-chain.yml; LICENSE (MIT); SECURITY.md absent from clone root; MDX-to-React compilation in docusaurus-mdx-loader

mermaid_diagrams_as_code.rationale: First-party theme package renders mermaid fences as React components with light/dark theme config, lazy loading, mermaid >=11.14 and optional ELK layouts; remark integration is in the core MDX pipeline. Client-side rendering (no static SVG) is the only caveat and does not affect JS-enabled readers.
mermaid_diagrams_as_code.evidence: packages/docusaurus-theme-mermaid/package.json (mermaid >=11.14.0, @mermaid-js/layout-elk peer); packages/docusaurus-mdx-loader/src/processor.ts (remark mermaid plugin); theme/Mermaid component in theme-classic MDXComponents

localization_bilingual.rationale: Built-in filesystem i18n needs no SaaS: per-locale file copies, write-translations extraction, locale dropdown and hreflang built into the theme; Hungarian theme translations exist upstream. Docked: HU coverage is partial (82/163 theme-common keys), translation is full-file duplication with no drift detection, and each locale roughly doubles build time.
localization_bilingual.evidence: packages/docusaurus/src/server/i18n.ts; packages/docusaurus-utils/src/i18nUtils.ts getPluginI18nPath; packages/docusaurus-theme-translations/locales/hu/ (5 of 5+ bundles, theme-common.json 82/163 keys); build --locale script in root package.json

deployment_self_hosting.rationale: Output is a plain static directory servable by any web server or CDN with zero runtime dependencies; first-party GitHub Pages deploy command, serve command for local hosting, and a hash-router mode for fully offline distribution. Nothing proprietary anywhere in the delivery path.
deployment_self_hosting.evidence: packages/docusaurus/src/commands/deploy.ts, serve.ts (serve-handler); packages/docusaurus/src/ssg/ (static HTML per route); experimental_router hash mode in packages/docusaurus-types/src/config.d.ts

dev_author_ux.rationale: Strong DX: typed TS config, hot reload, scaffolder, clear build errors, swizzle for theme customization, debug plugin; authors write plain MD/MDX in any editor with helpful frontmatter validation errors. Docked: MDX v3 strictness surprises authors, swizzled components create upgrade friction, no web editor for non-technical contributors, aggressive Node requirement.
dev_author_ux.evidence: packages/create-docusaurus; packages/docusaurus/src/commands/cli.ts (swizzle, start); packages/docusaurus-mdx-loader/src/format.ts (md/mdx detection, mdx1Compat); .github/workflows/tests-swizzle.yml (upstream mitigation of swizzle breakage)

search_seo.rationale: SEO is near best-in-class for an SSG: full static HTML, first-party sitemap with lastmod, per-page head control, hreflang alternates, throw-level broken-link enforcement. Search docked: first-party path is Algolia SaaS only; provider-independent local search requires third-party community plugins of varying quality.
search_seo.evidence: packages/docusaurus-plugin-sitemap/src/createSitemapItem.ts; theme-classic SiteMetadata/index.tsx (hreflang); packages/docusaurus/src/server/brokenLinks.ts; packages/docusaurus-theme-search-algolia (only search package in monorepo)

cost_efficiency.rationale: MIT-licensed, zero software cost, free static hosting tiers suffice, local search avoids SaaS fees; the only material costs are CI minutes (reduced by persistent caching) and the engineer's dependency-maintenance time.
cost_efficiency.evidence: LICENSE (MIT); static output model; future.faster caching flags in packages/docusaurus-types/src/config.d.ts

critical_constraints: Node >= 24.14 and React 19 required (packages/docusaurus/package.json engines) — constrains CI images and upgrade cadence
MDX v3 strict syntax: AI-generated content must be escaped/validated or builds fail; MDX is executable code requiring human review of generated PRs
Full rebuilds only — no true incremental SSG; warm-cache performance depends on opt-in future.faster flags (Rspack persistent cache)
Local/offline search requires community plugins; the only first-party search is Algolia SaaS
Hungarian theme translations upstream are ~50% complete; must be filled locally via write-translations
Mermaid renders client-side (no static SVG output) — diagrams invisible to no-JS consumers
verdict_one_liner: Adopt: the strongest mainstream fit for a GitHub-native, static-first, AI-augmented docs ecosystem — file-based everything, multi-instance content separation, first-party Mermaid and i18n — with manageable costs in npm surface, MDX strictness, and React-heavy output.
